example.en: The cook threw away foul food.
The seller took out a rotten fruit.

critique.note: خَبِيثَة is not the natural word for a rotten fruit (that is فَاسِدَة) and the gloss "rotten" misleads; use e.g. شَمَمْنَا رَائِحَةً خَبِيثَةً "We smelled a foul odor."

example.en: The food became foul.

critique.note: Food spoiling is فَسَدَ, not صَارَ خَبِيثًا; use a natural foul-water/smell context, e.g. صَارَ مَاءُ الْبِئْرِ خَبِيثًا.

example.en: The boy said foul words.
The neighbors warned us about a malicious woman.
example.bs: Komšije su nas upozorile na zlu ženu.

critique.note: Grammar and translations fine, but content is a negative judgment of a person (neighbors warning about a wicked woman) - gossip-like, not gentle everyday content; prefer e.g. a malicious plan/rumor or a foul smell (رَائِحَة خَبِيثَة).

example.en: The water in the well became foul.
example.bs: Voda u bunaru postala je pokvarena.

critique.note: خَبِيث for spoiled well water is not idiomatic MSA (one says آسِن / مُلَوَّث / فَسَدَ الْمَاءُ); use a natural collocation such as رَائِحَة خَبِيثَة or مَرَض خَبِيث.

example.en: This disease is malignant.

critique.note: Correct MSA (masc. agreement هذا/المرض/خبيثٌ, nominative tanwin). مرض خبيث = standard everyday term for malignant disease; zloćudna correctly agrees with feminine bolest. Sober but not harsh; not Quranic wording.
